submissionAttempts.body:
QUESTION: Which ordering guarantee applies to the workspace's integration (Palimpsest x Ordarium, via the shared local ledger) — "global" (Record A) or "per-consumer" (Record B)?

DETERMINATION: The guarantee is a single GLOBAL total order over committed state revisions in durable ledger commit-observation order, ascending. The feed cursor is a filter-independent durable position in that one shared order. Consumers may each retain their own cursor, but that is per-consumer resume bookkeeping into the same global order — not an independent per-consumer order. So Record A governs; Record B is incorrect as an ordering contract.

EVIDENCE (authoritative interface = the pinned integration surface, @ordarium/core 1.3.1 + @ordarium/ledger-sqlite 1.3.1, per package.json: dependencies and pnpm-workspace.yaml overrides, both 1.3.1, and the installed node_modules):
1. core/dist/src/types.d.ts (StateChangePage/StateChangeFeed, ORD-BOOT-0): "One page of committed state revisions in durable ledger commit-observation order, ascending (ORD-BOOT-0)"; cursor is an "Opaque, filter-independent durable position of the last delivered change"; StateChangeFilter is only a namespace narrowing; StateChangePage.cursor is always present ("a consumer reaches the end of the feed and still holds a durable resume position").
2. core/dist/src/ledger.js changes(): positions are contiguous 1..n in one ledger-wide array (#stateChanges); the cursor decodes to a single numeric position; a cursor beyond the ledger's own global history throws InvalidCursorError ("fail closed", never a per-consumer restart).
3. ledger-sqlite/dist/src/index.js changes(): SQL is filter on "c.change_seq > ?" plus optional namespace, "ORDER BY c.change_seq ASC"; comment: "Semantic validation against the global high-water mark (ORD-BOOT-0.1): the cursor is a global, filter-independent position, so this compares against the whole ledger, not the requested namespace's last sequence."
4. Same file, compareAndSetState: "The ordering row is assigned by the database inside this same transaction (ORD-BOOT-0): a committed revision and its observable change position are never split, and a rolled-back CAS leaves neither." (ordering is a ledger-wide DB sequence, atomic with commit).
5. ledger-sqlite/dist/src/migrations.js: "change_seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT"; v3->v4 migration note: "v3 recorded no global commit order... From v4 on, every new commit carries the real durable database order."
6. core/dist/src/errors.js InvalidCursorError: a non-decodable/foreign cursor "refusing to guess a resume point" — i.e., the cursor is a position in one global order, not a private per-consumer sequence.

DECISION RATIONALE / PROVENANCE: The two local files docs/engineering/09-ordering-contract-a.md ("global") and 09-ordering-contract-b.md ("per-consumer") assert mutually exclusive, identically styled normative claims for the same "current pinned line". They are supplied by neither the engineering-archive index (docs/engineering/README.md lists the 00-36 records; these two are absent and unreferenced anywhere) nor the SDS; they are not specs, and the file number also collides with the real 09-adaptive-allocation-spec.md. More decisively, docs/engineering/07-ordarium-alignment.md establishes that the Ordarium contract is authoritative in its own domain ("Ordarium 合同以其仓库 docs/12–17 为准") and that Palimpsest consumes Ordarium only through the public contract surface (§0/§1). The pinned 1.3.1 release artifacts ARE that surface and implement ORD-BOOT-0 unambiguously as a single global, filter-independent commit-observation order. Therefore the conflict resolves locally by an explicit source-precedence rule (consumer-side records cannot redefine the producer's feed contract) plus the binding pinned artifact; Record B simply mistakes the consumer's own resume cursor for an independent order. No peer contact is needed because no load-bearing source remains genuinely unresolved — the peer's own pinned contract surface already answers it.

DISPOSITION: unresolved — the ordering guarantee cannot yet be fixed as an accepted cross-boundary fact.

WHAT IS UNDERDETERMINED: Two Palimpsest-local records assert mutually exclusive normative claims about the state-change feed ordering for the same "current pinned line":
- docs/engineering/09-ordering-contract-a.md — "global: one position shared by all readers of the store";
- docs/engineering/09-ordering-contract-b.md — "per-consumer: each consumer holds its own independent position."
Both are load-bearing (each claims normative/current scope) and both are unreferenced elsewhere in a workspace of ~10,000 files. Neither is listed in docs/engineering/README.md's archive index, and their number collides with the real record 09-adaptive-allocation-spec.md. No local doc picks a winner, and this proposition is about the Ordarium feed contract, not a Palimpsest-owned artifact.

WHY LOCAL PRECEDENCE IS NOT ENOUGH: docs/engineering/07-ordarium-alignment.md (PLMP-ALN-1, marked as the cross-repo coordination authority) fixes the documentary authority order: "Ordarium 合同以其仓库 docs/12–17 为准 ... 跨域冲突以本文登记的裁决为准并双向同步". docs/engineering/08-telemetry-externalization-spec.md names the feed's sibling authority explicitly: "对侧合同：Ordarium docs/17 §16.6 (G11) 与 @ordarium/core state 合同面". docs/engineering/00-heritage.md adds: "Ordarium 侧合同 ... 以 Ordarium 仓库 docs/12–17 与 evidence/ 为准；本仓库不复制其文本，只引用." Those canonical texts are not present in this workspace, and their owner is ordarium.main. My own engineering README's precedence rule covers SDS-vs-product-doc conflicts only; it does not authorize a Palimpsest-side record to fix the producer's feed contract. So the boundary having authority over this proposition has not participated.

LOCAL EVIDENCE (leaning, not authoritative): The pinned integration surface (@ordarium/core 1.3.1 and @ordarium/ledger-sqlite 1.3.1, per package.json + pnpm-workspace.yaml + node_modules) reads as a single global order:
- types.d.ts StateChangePage: "durable ledger commit-observation order, ascending (ORD-BOOT-0)"; cursor: "Opaque, filter-independent durable position"; StateChangeFilter only narrows by namespace.
- ledger.js changes(): one ledger-wide position array, contiguous 1..n; a cursor past the ledger's history throws InvalidCursorError.
- ledger-sqlite index.js changes(): "ORDER BY c.change_seq ASC"; comment "the cursor is a global, filter-independent position, so this compares against the whole ledger, not the requested namespace's last sequence"; compareAndSetState assigns change_seq in the same transaction ("a committed revision and its observable change position are never split"); migrations.js: change_seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT and "v3 recorded no global commit order ... from v4 on every new commit carries the real durable database order".
That strongly indicates Record A (global) and makes Record B look like a conflation of a consumer's own resume cursor with an independent order. But "the code I can see reads this way" is exactly the kind of source the admission policy treats as insufficient for an owning peer's contract surface, so I am not asserting it as resolved.

ACTIONS TAKEN TO OBTAIN THE AUTHORITY: I opened thread thr_49f4804a-0374-42e9-9faf-9f49e6edac8a with ordarium.main — a question (evt_750fd5e8) and a blocking need (evt_e71d57a0), each asking for one normative yes/no plus citation and applicable revision. I proposed the boundary contract plmp-ordarium-statechange-feed-ordering@1 to hold the answer and the acceptance criteria; it is still draft with acceptedBy empty. Inbox polls returned no peer events.

CLOSING CONDITION: a single accepted/authoritative boundary event from ordarium.main naming the guarantee with its normative citation and revision (or a peer-accepted revision of the contract above). On receipt I can immediately re-dispose: if global, mark 09-ordering-contract-b.md non-authoritative and keep A; if per-consumer, the reverse; either way both records must not both stand.

finalAnswerPreview: The owning peer has not yet provided an authoritative answer. Given the policy block, the honest disposition is unresolved — but let me first make one more attempt to reach the peer with an explicit need, and re-poll.
